title: Clean trombone technique and the high-pitch horn
summary: He explains playing cleanly, short positions, and how a high-pitch horn taught him to play in odd keys, plus hillbilly band experience.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well, I remember when I was a little kid, uh, hearing, uh, the trombone, I used to think they were just murdering the instrument by sliding around on the trombone. And, uh, initially they were, they were just hunting for the note, you know, and, uh, they would just clown it up when they couldn't find it. And, I always thought that if I couldn't play it clean and right, I wasn't going to play it at all. And, uh, of course I learned a lot of shortcuts because in, in my early years my arms weren't very long. And I had to make, uh, uh, different, uh, positions and things that, uh, in some notes, in the lower positions, I had to leave out entirely. And, uh, then one fortunate thing, uh, I started on a high pitch horn. It used to have two, uh, different, uh, standard pitches. There was one called standard and there was one called international or orchestra pitch. And they were half a tone apart. Well, I had the wrong horn. I had the high pitch horn. I was playing it with the piano. So, I learned to play in, uh, when the piano was in B flat, I'd be in A. And, uh, when the piano was in F, I'd be in E. And, I think that, uh, turned out to be a fortunate mistake instead of a holdback. Because, now I can look back at those keys that I used to have to play in, and it makes it come easier now. You played with, uh, string, you said, with the hillbilly band, too. They play in a lot of sharp keys. Yeah, yes, they do. And, uh, see, I was the only instrument up in that thinly populated area in Vernon and San Angelo. I'd be the only instrument, you know, besides piano and banjo and drums. So, uh, I could play the melody and, uh, and play a chorus, that lib. And when you play it in turkey and straw and things like that, it's really technical. You know, it's a, it's a kind of a hillbilly. I mean, it's not too easy. Well, it, uh, I think it was a good start. Rather, it'd be, it was kind of crude, but it was a good start for a person that had to be self-taught.
